critical_code_review_comments: AssignmentsTab.js:340 — DialogContent `max-w-2xl max-h-[90vh] flex flex-col p-0` correctly caps the dialog. Header (px-6 pt-6 pb-2 flex-shrink-0 border-b) and Footer (px-6 py-4 flex-shrink-0 border-t bg-white) are properly pinned. Body div (data-testid=assignment-form-body) `flex-1 overflow-y-auto min-h-0` is the correct pattern to make a flex-col child scroll. LGTM.

AssignmentsTab.js:381-395 & 404-416 — Inline save button is passed via `inlineSaveButton` prop for both create and edit modes; both variants use the SAME data-testid `assignment-form-inline-save-btn` (per contract) and share the same `handleSave` handler with the footer button. LGTM.

SubmissionTypeFields.js:22, 80 — `inlineSaveButton = null` default is safe; renders in a `flex items-center gap-2` container so it sits next to the Add Question button. Only rendered inside the questionnaire builder (`isQuestionnaire` branch), so it correctly disappears when submission_type ≠ business_questionnaire. LGTM.

MaterialLibrary.js:338, 343, 481 — Same scroll pattern applied to the upload DialogContent. Inline save (`lib-upload-inline-save-btn`) is gated on `form.material_type === 'homework' && form.submission_type === 'business_questionnaire'`. LGTM.

MINOR (pre-existing, not related to this fix): AssignmentsTab.js:397 renders a SECOND SubmissionTypeFields component when editing a questionnaire assignment, with `onSubmissionTypeChange={() => {}}`. That means the Select dropdown for Homework Format still appears in edit mode but is a no-op — confusing UX. The submission_type genuinely cannot be changed post-create (backend PUT drops it), but the disabled state should be indicated visually or the Select hidden in edit mode. Recommend hiding the format selector in edit mode.

context_for_next_testing_agent: This iteration was PURE FRONTEND (CSS + one new prop). No backend changes. If regression-testing, the important measurement is: after selecting business_questionnaire and adding 15+ questions, `document.querySelector('[data-testid="assignment-form-body"]').scrollHeight` should exceed the viewport minus header/footer, while the DialogContent element's height remains capped at ~90vh AND the footer save-btn's getBoundingClientRect().bottom stays ≤ window.innerHeight. Verified live on preview URL. Note: cohort route is `/cohort/:cohortId` (singular), library is `/library` (not /material-library). Library 'Add Material' button (not 'Add to Library').
rca of the issue: USER BUG: DialogContent had no max-height/overflow so growing the questionnaire pushed the DialogFooter (Save button) past the viewport, unreachable. FIX correctly implemented in AssignmentsTab.js:340 and MaterialLibrary.js:338 by (a) adding `max-h-[90vh] flex flex-col p-0` to DialogContent, (b) making header & footer `flex-shrink-0` so they retain size, (c) making the body `flex-1 overflow-y-auto min-h-0` so it absorbs excess height and scrolls internally. VERIFIED: at 18 questions the body's scrollHeight was 2304px but the dialog remained 810px and the footer stayed at y=802-838 (visible in 900px viewport). Bonus 'Save Progress' inline button (data-testid `assignment-form-inline-save-btn` / `lib-upload-inline-save-btn`) wired via a new `inlineSaveButton` prop on SubmissionTypeFields — appears only in questionnaire builder header next to 'Add Question', calls the same save handler, respects saving/disabled state.
